papers.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
papers.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic,
papers.summary: The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform that packages over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers for researchers analyzing the explosion of microbial omics data, covering metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, and (meta)transcriptomic analyses.

papers.title: From saccharides to methane: substrate-driven microbial diversity and methanogenesis in anaerobic digestion revealed by 390 MAGs.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) is a key technology for organic waste treatment and renewable energy production, yet its microbial processes remain poorly understood. This study employed genome-centric metagenomics to investigate synthetic AD systems fed with five substrates: starch, glucose, butyrate, propionate-valerate, and acetate. A total of 390 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were reconstructed, 64.36% of which represent potentially novel species. Substrate-driven selection shaped distinct functional consortia, with Bifidobacterium enriched in starch hydrolysis and Syntrophomon
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed 390 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes from synthetic anaerobic digestion systems fed with five different substrates, finding that substrate type strongly selects for distinct microbial consortia and functional guilds. Over 64% of the recovered MAGs represent potentially novel species, and specific taxa (e.g., Bifidobacterium for starch hydrolysis, Syntrophomonas for butyrate) were enriched in substrate-specific roles. This genome-centric resource expands the known diversity of AD microbiomes and links substrate chemistry to methanogenesis pathways.

papers.title: Taxonova: Deep learning enables fast and confidence-aware microbiome species-level amplicon classification.
papers.abstract: Accurate species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences remains challenging due to the difficulty of resolving subtle variations within conserved ribosomal regions. Traditional similarity-based methods struggle with short amplicons and sequences with poor database representation. No existing method performs robustly across the full spectrum of amplicon lengths, limiting applicability across diverse sequencing platforms and variable-region targets. We present Taxonova, a deep learning framework for both short- and long-read ribosomal amplicons. Evaluated across physical
papers.summary: Taxonova is a deep learning framework that classifies microbial amplicon sequences at the species level for both short- and long-read sequencing platforms. It addresses the limitations of similarity-based methods, which struggle with short amplicons and poorly represented taxa, by providing confidence-aware predictions across diverse amplicon lengths and variable regions.

papers.title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures.
papers.abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited in
papers.summary: This study longitudinally profiles the upper respiratory virome of beef calves from birth to weaning, revealing that viral communities are dynamic and include phage-driven adaptation. The findings highlight cross-host evolutionary signatures, suggesting cattle respiratory viromes may serve as a reservoir for viruses with zoonotic potential at the human-animal interface.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: The authors constructed the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic strain Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, using a new nutrient-controlled reconstruction approach. They also established comprehensive nutrient requirements for well-controlled in vitro growth studies and analyzed secretion products. This provides a more accurate metabolic framework for studying this widely used gut commensal.

papers.title: CNTN4: A Possible Candidate Gene for Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota plays a significant role in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), though findings vary substantially across studies. Using gut microbiome data from a genome-wide association study of 5,959 participants and summary statistics from 46,351 ASD and 55,374 ADHD cases, we conducted bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses with inverse variance weighting as the primary method. Reverse MR analysis assessed potential reverse causality. We annotated single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with SNP-nexus to identify associated ge
papers.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization to test bidirectional causal relationships between gut microbiome composition and risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ADHD, leveraging large GWAS summary statistics. The authors identified CNTN4 as a possible candidate gene linking the microbiota-gut-brain axis to both neurodevelopmental conditions. The findings suggest shared genetic pathways may underlie microbiome-mediated risk for ASD and ADHD, though the candidate gene evidence is preliminary.

papers.title: Modeling association networks from metagenome time series - a proof-of-concept from two contrasting estuaries.
papers.abstract: Understanding microbial responses to environmental gradients is important for ecosystem assessment in estuarine environments. Here, we integrated time-series samples and shotgun metagenomics with association network inference, to examine patterns of taxonomic and functional co-variation. We collected and sequenced eDNA from two sediment time series from neighbouring but environmentally contrasting Basque estuaries, and compared the resulting taxonomic and functional association networks, based on Metagenome Assembled Genomes (MAGs) and KEGG Orthologous Groups (KOs), respectively. Networks infe
papers.summary: The authors combined time-series sediment eDNA sampling with shotgun metagenomics and association network inference to compare taxonomic and functional co-variation patterns in two neighbouring but environmentally contrasting Basque estuaries. Networks were built from Metagenome Assembled Genomes (MAGs) and KEGG Orthologous Groups (KOs), providing a proof-of-concept for linking microbial community structure to function across environmental gradients.

papers.title: Bacterial community profiles of soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve, Philippines.
papers.abstract: The Mount Makiling Forest Reserve harbors diverse microorganisms with potential biotechnological applications, yet bacterial taxonomic profiling across its watersheds remains limited. Amplicon metagenome sequencing targeting the 16S rRNA gene revealed Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota as dominant phyla, with Actinobacteriota, Verrucomicrobiota, Chloroflexi, Myxococcota, Methylomirabilota, Bacteroidota, Nitrospirota, and Planctomycetota present at varying abundances.
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to profile bacterial communities in soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve in the Philippines. Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota were the dominant phyla, with ten additional phyla present at varying abundances across watersheds. The work provides a baseline taxonomic survey of an understudied tropical forest soil microbiome.

papers.title: Causal effects between gut microbiology and hyperlipidemia: A 2-sample Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Recent studies have confirmed the connection between gut microbiota (GM) and hyperlipidemia. This study used the Mendelian randomization (MR) technique to explore the association between GM and hyperlipidemia. MR was used to examine data derived from a genome-wide association study that combined data from 211 intestinal microbiota and hyperlipidemia. Five statistical tools were used for statistical analyses, including the MR-Egger method, the weighted median method, the inverse variance weighted method, the simple model, and the weighted mode. Inverse variance weighted is the main type among t
papers.summary: This study applied two-sample Mendelian randomization to test whether gut microbiome composition causally affects hyperlipidemia risk, using GWAS summary data for 211 microbial taxa and hyperlipidemia. Multiple MR methods (primarily inverse-variance weighted) were used to estimate causal effects. The work adds to a growing body of MR-based evidence linking specific gut microbes to lipid disorders, though the abstract does not report specific causal taxa or effect sizes.

papers.title: Hospital Drain Microbiomes as Distinct Microbial Signatures Within Urban Wastewater Networks in the Han River Watershed.
papers.abstract: Background: Hospital drainage systems represent an important interface between healthcare facilities and urban wastewater networks and may contribute distinct microbial inputs to downstream aquatic environments. This issue is particularly relevant in Seoul, Republic of Korea, where urban wastewater discharges into receiving waters within the Han River watershed. Methods: In this study, we characterized hospital drain microbiomes to evaluate their microbial and environmental signatures, using residential drains as a non-clinical comparison. Results: Hospital drains exhibited a distinct taxonomi
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiomes of hospital drains with residential drains in Seoul's Han River watershed, finding that hospital drains harbor distinct taxonomic signatures. The results suggest hospital drainage systems introduce unique microbial inputs into urban wastewater networks that differ from non-clinical sources.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Mammals' Health: Integrating Multi-Omics Data for Precision Nutrition and Sustainable Production.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition in modern mammalian production aims to transition from static feeding regimens toward dynamic and customized strategies by unraveling complex interactions among genetics, environment, the gut microbiome, and host physiology. Machine learning provides a powerful analytical framework to navigate high-dimensional multi-omics datasets. However, existing applications frequently lack systematic criteria for algorithm selection and remain largely confined to observational statistical associations without progressing toward causal verification. This perspective delineates a coheren
papers.summary: This perspective argues that precision nutrition for mammalian production should move beyond static feeding regimens by integrating multi-omics data (genetics, microbiome, physiology) through machine learning. The authors highlight that current ML applications often lack systematic algorithm-selection criteria and remain limited to observational associations rather than causal validation, and they propose a coherent framework to address these gaps.

papers.title: Shenqi Granules Ameliorate Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Glucocerebrosidase and Uridine Metabolism in Microglia.
papers.abstract: Objective: Shenqi Granules is a traditional Chinese medicine formula derived from the classic prescription Shenqi Formula (SQF), composed of Astragali Radix (Huangqi) and Codonopsis Radix (Dangshen). SQF shows neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: The rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established using the suture method to evaluate the neuroprotective effect of SQF. Blood-absorbed components were identified via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, and potential targets and pathways were predicted through netw
papers.summary: This study shows that Shenqi Granules, a traditional Chinese medicine formula, protect against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats by acting on microglia. Using network pharmacology and metabolomics, the authors link the protective effect to regulation of glucocerebrosidase and uridine metabolism in these brain immune cells.

papers.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Metabolic Phenotyping and Precision Nutrition: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has evolved beyond conventional diabetes management into an enabling technology for metabolic phenotyping and precision nutrition by providing continuous, real-world assessment of individual glycemic responses to dietary and lifestyle exposures. This narrative review examines the principles and clinical utility of CGM and its emerging applications in metabolic monitoring and personalized nutrition, with particular emphasis on postprandial glycemic variability, computational prediction, dietary feedback, and behavioral interventions. A literature search was c
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has expanded beyond diabetes care into metabolic phenotyping and precision nutrition, focusing on postprandial glycemic variability, computational prediction of glucose responses, and dietary/behavioral feedback interventions. It synthesizes current evidence on CGM's clinical utility and discusses future directions for personalized nutrition. The review is descriptive rather than presenting new data.

papers.title: Next-Generation Functional Nanoplatforms: Engineering Plant-Derived Extracellular Vesicles for Targeted Bioactive Delivery and Health Applications.
papers.abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) are being recognized as a capable novel class of natural nanocarriers that have important uses in delivering bioactives and facilitating innovations in functional foods and precision health technologies. PDEVs are lipid-bilayer-enclosed vesicular structures that commonly occur at the nanoscale, although their reported sizes vary depending on the plant source, isolation procedure, and measurement method. They contain diverse biomolecules, including lipids, proteins, microRNAs, and phytochemicals, and have been investigated for their potential roles i
papers.summary: This review discusses plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) as natural nanocarriers for delivering bioactive compounds, highlighting their lipid-bilayer structure, variable nanoscale sizes, and cargo of lipids, proteins, microRNAs, and phytochemicals. The authors examine engineering strategies to enhance PDEVs for targeted delivery and applications in functional foods and precision health. The work synthesizes current knowledge on isolation methods, characterization challenges, and translational potential.

papers.title: Multikingdom and functional gut microbiota markers for cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While the association between gut microbiota and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) has been explored, existing research has been limited to bacterial components. The alterations in non-bacterial members (fungi, archaea, and viruses) and their functional characteristics in CCA remain unclear. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the multi-kingdom gut microbiota and functional profiles in CCA patients and develop a non-invasive diagnostic model.
papers.summary: This study comprehensively characterizes the multi-kingdom gut microbiota—including bacteria, fungi, archaea, and viruses—along with functional profiles in patients with cholangiocarcinoma, moving beyond prior work that focused only on bacteria. The authors use these multi-kingdom and functional markers to develop a non-invasive diagnostic model for CCA.

papers.title: Identification of Genes Associated with Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Complicated by Acute Cerebral Infarction Based on Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and acute cerebral infarction (ACI) are globally prevalent diseases that impose substantial public health burdens. While gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognized to regulate metabolic and immune homeostasis linked to both diseases, its shared genetically predicted microbial taxa and underlying metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms in T2DM and ACI remain unclear, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to elucidate their regulatory mechanisms. Methods: Transcriptomic datasets, genome-wide association stu
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with Mendelian randomization to identify gut microbiota taxa and metabolites that may causally influence the shared risk of type 2 diabetes and acute cerebral infarction. The authors link genetically predicted microbial features to candidate genes, proposing metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms underlying both diseases. The work is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, with findings requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Exploratory Shotgun Metagenomic Analysis of the Fecal Microbiome and Antimicrobial-Resistance Potential in Simmental Calves with Different Diarrheal Statuses.
papers.abstract: Calf diarrhea is frequently accompanied by disruption of the gastrointestinal microbiota, but the relationships between clinical status and microbial community composition, gene-content functional potential, and antimicrobial-resistance-associated features remain incompletely characterized. This exploratory study aimed to characterize these features in calves with different diarrheal statuses using shotgun metagenomics. Six approximately 2-month-old Simmental calves from Chahar Right Middle Banner, Inner Mongolia, were included, comprising two healthy calves, two calves with mild diarrhea, and
papers.summary: This exploratory study used shotgun metagenomics to compare fecal microbiome composition, functional gene content, and antimicrobial-resistance potential in six Simmental calves with different diarrheal statuses (healthy, mild diarrhea, and presumably more severe diarrhea). The small sample size limits statistical power, but the work characterizes how clinical status relates to microbial community and resistance-gene features in calves.

papers.title: Limited Gut Microbiome Differences Between Relapsing-Remitting and Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Shotgun Metagenomic Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome may contribute to multiple sclerosis (MS) pathophysiology, but its relationship with disease phenotype and progression remains unclear. To characterize taxonomic and functional gut microbiome differences between relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) and secondary progressive MS (SPMS) and their associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers. This cross-sectional study included 89 participants (30 healthy controls, 29 RRMS, and 30 SPMS). Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to assess microbial diversity, taxonomic profiles, and predefined short-chain fatty ac
papers.summary: This cross-sectional shotgun metagenomic study compared gut microbiome composition across 30 healthy controls, 29 relapsing-remitting MS patients, and 30 secondary progressive MS patients. The authors found only limited taxonomic and functional differences between RRMS and SPMS, suggesting that gut microbiome signatures do not strongly distinguish disease phenotype or track with progression. Associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers were modest at best.

papers.title: From Microbiome Associations to Deployable Precision Probiotics in Animals: A Critical Narrative Review and Proposed Causal Evidence Framework for Next-Generation Probiotic Development.
papers.abstract: Next-generation probiotics (NGPs) are promoted as precision tools for animal health, yet the term is often applied to uncommon taxa before causality, safety and target-species efficacy are established. This critical narrative review reframes animal NGPs as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic category. A structured PubMed search was last run on 14 September 2026 with a publication date cutoff of 1 September 2026 and was supplemented by citation tracing and targeted searches of authoritative sources. From the screened literature, 45 representative and conceptually informative sources w
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This critical narrative review argues that "next-generation probiotics" for animals should be defined as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic label, since many candidate taxa are promoted before causality, safety, and target-species efficacy are established. Drawing on 45 representative sources, the authors propose a causal evidence framework to guide the progression from microbiome association to deployable precision probiotics. The review emphasizes rigorous causal validation as a prerequisite for translating microbiome findings into animal health products.

papers.title: Rethinking Solid-Phase Microextraction (SPME) for Bioanalysis: Workflow Optimisation in Automated Vacuum-Assisted Cooling SPME for Fatty Acid Monitoring in Faecal Waters.
papers.abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are key biomarkers of gut microbiota and intestinal health, yet their analysis is challenging due to high volatility, hydrophilicity, and the complexity of the faecal matrix. This study introduces a novel, green, and fully automated workflow for monitoring SCFAs in faecal water samples. It combines microwave-assisted derivatisation, vacuum-assisted cooling multiple solid-phase microextraction (Vac-HS-cooling-MSPME), and fast gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). On-sample derivatisation with 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzyl bromide was optimised via design of
papers.summary: This study develops a fully automated, green analytical workflow for measuring short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in faecal water, combining microwave-assisted derivatisation with vacuum-assisted cooling multiple solid-phase microextraction (Vac-HS-cooling-MSPME) and fast GC-MS. The optimised method addresses the volatility, hydrophilicity, and matrix complexity challenges of SCFA analysis, offering a streamlined approach for monitoring these gut microbiota biomarkers.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a
papers.summary: This review outlines the network pharmacology workflow for studying natural products, covering active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation, target prediction, network construction, and pathway enrichment, with molecular docking and experimental validation as complementary steps. It emphasizes how systems-level integration of chemical, biological, and disease data can clarify the multi-target mechanisms of complex natural product mixtures.

papers.title: Dynamics of Gut Microbial Community and Function in Growing Male Raccoon Dogs.
papers.abstract: Background: Raccoon dogs have short breeding cycles and strong adaptability, and their fur is economically valuable. Although the gut microbiota, a key regulator of animal health, has been extensively studied in livestock, its composition and function in raccoon dogs remain poorly understood. Methods: In this study, the gut microbiota structure and functional profiles of ten raccoon dogs were analyzed during their growth period, including 2 (M2), 3 (M3), 4 (M4), 6 (M6), and 8 (M8) months after birth. Results: Our findings revealed that the richness and diversity of the gut microbiota in growin
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study tracked gut microbiota composition and functional profiles in ten male raccoon dogs across five time points from 2 to 8 months of age. The authors report changes in microbial richness and diversity during growth, providing a first characterization of how the gut microbiome develops in this species. The work is largely descriptive and focused on a non-model, economically relevant fur animal.

papers.title: Integrated Metagenomic and Metatranscriptomic Analysis Reveals Microbiome Differences Between Bisexual and Parthenogenetic Populations of Haemaphysalis longicornis.
papers.abstract: The tick Haemaphysalis longicornis is an important vector of human and animal pathogens in East Asia that comprises both bisexual (Bis) and parthenogenetic (Par) populations. While previous studies have documented differences between these reproductive groups in genome ploidy, host transcription, and vector capacity, it remains unclear whether reproductive strategy is accompanied by systematic divergence in the tick-associated microbiome, including microbial community composition, transcriptional activities, and functional outputs. Here, we profiled laboratory-maintained Bis and Par population
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiome of bisexual and parthenogenetic populations of the tick Haemaphysalis longicornis using integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing. The authors found systematic differences in microbial community composition and transcriptional activity between the two reproductive groups, suggesting that reproductive strategy is associated with distinct microbiome functional outputs. These findings highlight a link between tick reproductive biology and vector-associated microbial ecology.

papers.title: Traditional Food Use and Ethnomedicinal Contexts of Turnip (Brassica rapa L.): A Scoping Review of Composition, Food Processing, and Health-Related Evidence.
papers.abstract: Turnip (Brassica rapa L.) is widely cultivated for food and has documented ethnomedicinal uses. This scoping review mapped the international literature on turnip, with detailed synthesis focused on turnip materials associated with selected regional food and ethnomedicinal traditions in China. Searches covered seven bibliographic databases. The bibliographic map comprised 771 records, of which 397 were selected for detailed synthesis. Regional uses varied in plant part and preparation method. The clearest evidence concerned composition and processing: constituent profiles differed by provenance
papers.summary: This scoping review mapped 771 records on turnip (Brassica rapa), synthesizing 397 in detail, with a focus on regional food and ethnomedicinal traditions in China. The strongest evidence concerned how plant part, preparation method, and provenance shape constituent profiles, while health-related evidence was less well developed. It provides a structured overview of composition, processing, and traditional use rather than new experimental findings.

papers.title: Soil Microbiome Signatures Associated with Epidemiological Heterogeneity Across Natural Plague Foci in Inner Mongolia, China.
papers.abstract: Plague persistence relies on complex host-vector-environment interactions, yet the ecological contribution of soil microbiomes to natural foci remains poorly understood. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples across four distinct plague foci in Inner Mongolia, China, to characterize microbiome features associated with contrasting epidemiological states. Taxonomic, functional, and network analyses showed that the three active plague foci exhibited lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa, particularly Streptomyces. Co
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples from four plague foci in Inner Mongolia revealed that the three epidemiologically active foci had lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa such as Streptomyces compared with the inactive focus. The study links soil microbiome structure and function to contrasting plague epidemiological states, suggesting the soil microbiome may be an ecological factor in plague persistence.

papers.title: Elevated Level of Fannyhessea vaginae Correlated with Implantation Outcomes in Women undergoing in vitro fertilization Treatment.
papers.abstract: The vaginal microbiome plays a significant role in reproductive health. While maintaining a balanced vaginal microbiome is crucial for successful in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, the specific bacteria associated with adverse outcomes may vary by region and are largely unknown. This study aims to investigate the bacterial profiles and their influence on embryo implantation, thereby supporting the development of microbiome-based therapies. One hundred women undergoing IVF provided vaginal swabs at three stages: oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and hCG pregnancy testing. An in-house 16S r
papers.summary: This study profiled the vaginal microbiome of 100 women undergoing IVF at three time points (oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and pregnancy testing) using 16S rRNA sequencing. Higher abundance of Fannyhessea vaginae was associated with poorer embryo implantation outcomes, suggesting this bacterium may serve as a marker or target for microbiome-based interventions to improve IVF success.

papers.title: Dietary Fibre in Pea Cotyledon Used as a Protein Source Provides Multidimensional Protection Against Colonic Protein Putrefaction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Substitution of plant-based for animal-based protein sources has been recommended to reduce global non-communicable disease burdens, including colorectal cancer. Objective: The goal of this study was to determine possible ways that pea cotyledon may modulate hindgut concentrations of protein putrefaction products implicated in colorectal cancer by comparing diets based on casein, meat or pea cotyledon in a rat model. Method: Rats (n = 8 per treatment) were fed for 9 days on 18.6% protein diets containing casein, meat, or yellow split peas as sole protein sources. Faecal
papers.summary: In a rat feeding trial, a diet using yellow split pea cotyledon as the sole protein source reduced hindgut markers of protein putrefaction compared with casein- or meat-based diets. The pea diet's fibre content appears to provide multidimensional protection against colonic protein fermentation products linked to colorectal cancer risk.

papers.title: Short-Term Simulated NH4+/NO3- Inputs Reorganize Soil Microbial Communities and Modify N-Cycling Functional Potential in Temperate Forests.
papers.abstract: Forest soil nitrogen (N) turnover and nitrous oxide (N2O) release are strongly influenced by atmospheric N deposition. Although the effects of individual inorganic N species on soil biogeochemistry are well documented, the consequences of changing their relative supply for N2O formation and the underlying microbial pathways remain less clear. We therefore examined soil N2O emissions, microbial communities, and N-transformation potential across a gradient of ammonium-to-nitrate (NH4+/NO3-) inputs in a temperate forest soil from Northeast China. Seven treatments covering NH4+/NO3- ratios from 1:
papers.summary: This study tested how different ratios of ammonium to nitrate inputs affect soil microbial communities and nitrogen cycling in temperate forest soil from Northeast China. The authors found that shifting the NH4+/NO3- balance reorganizes microbial community composition and alters the functional potential for nitrogen transformations, with implications for nitrous oxide emissions. The work highlights that the relative supply of inorganic N species, not just total N load, shapes soil biogeochemical responses.

papers.title: Intratumoral Bacterial Profiles, Bacterial Co-Detection Patterns, and Molecular Alterations in Colorectal Cancer and Colorectal Polyps: A Vietnamese Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Intratumoral microbiota may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC), but their relationships with bacterial co-occurrence, relative bacterial loads, and molecular alterations remain incompletely understood. This study characterized intratumoral bacterial profiles in CRC and colorectal polyps and examined their clinicopathological and molecular associations. A cross-sectional study included 149 patients with CRC and 109 patients with benign colorectal polyps. F. nucleatum, ETBF, A. muciniphila, and eae+E. coli were detected in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues using multiplex real-time PC
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study profiled intratumoral bacteria (F. nucleatum, enterotoxigenic B. fragilis, A. muciniphila, and eae+ E. coli) in colorectal cancer and benign polyp tissues from a Vietnamese cohort using multiplex real-time PCR. It examined how bacterial detection patterns relate to co-occurrence, bacterial load, and molecular/clinicopathological features. The work adds population-specific data on tumor-associated microbiota in colorectal neoplasia.

papers.title: Synovial SLC1A5-Associated Amino Acid Metabolic Features in Knee Osteoarthritis: An Integrated Analysis of Synovial Transcriptomics, Fecal Metabolomics, and Gut Microbiota.
papers.abstract: Background: This exploratory study aimed to characterize amino acid related features in osteoarthritis (OA). Methods: We analyzed independent public synovial transcriptomic datasets and paired fecal metabolomics and 16S ribosomal RNA profiles from 20 patients with knee OA and 14 controls. Metabolite-sensing genes were intersected with nominally differential genes and prioritized using elastic net, support vector machine recursive feature elimination, and extreme gradient boosting. Results:SLC1A5 (solute carrier family 1 member 5) expression was lower in the discovery cohort GSE89408 (log2 fold
papers.summary: This exploratory study integrated public synovial transcriptomic data with paired fecal metabolomics and 16S rRNA profiles from 20 knee osteoarthritis patients and 14 controls to identify amino acid metabolic features. The solute carrier gene SLC1A5 emerged as a prioritized metabolite-sensing gene with lower expression in OA synovium, and the work links synovial amino acid metabolism to gut microbiota and fecal metabolite profiles. The findings are preliminary and based on small, cross-sectional cohorts, so they suggest hypotheses rather than establish causal mechanisms.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium longum Depletion and Bile Acid Dysregulation in MASLD: Links to Hepatic TGR5-AMPK Signaling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis and aberrant bile acid metabolism are central to MASLD pathogenesis, the critical keystone species and precise molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of 14 public 16S rRNA datasets (275 controls, 352 patients), combining multi-method differential abundance screening, machine learning, and network analysis to pinpoint MASLD-specific microbial signatures. We further validated the therapeutic potential of can
papers.summary: This study integrated 14 public 16S rRNA datasets to identify Bifidobacterium longum as a key species depleted in MASLD, alongside bile acid dysregulation. The authors link this depletion to altered hepatic TGR5-AMPK signaling and suggest that restoring B. longum may have therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Microbiome-Related Amino-Acid Profiles of Liver and Muscle Tissues in Arbor Acres Broiler Chickens.
papers.abstract: The study, designed as a group-level integrative data analysis, included homogeneous datasets obtained from 24 Arbor Acres chicken groups. Quantitative amino-acid analysis in chicken tissues was carried out using the capillary electrophoresis method. Gut microbial community analysis was performed using 16S rRNA gene-sequencing technology on the Illumina MiSeq platform. Amino-acid analysis of liver samples revealed 10 Arg-high and 14 Arg-low chicken groups, while for thigh samples, the ratio of Arg-high and Arg-low groups was 18/6, respectively. The gut microbiomes of chickens with an Arg-high
papers.summary: This study profiled amino acids in liver and thigh muscle of Arbor Acres broiler chickens and linked them to gut microbiome composition using 16S rRNA sequencing. Groups were classified as arginine-high or arginine-low based on tissue amino-acid levels, and microbiome differences were examined between these groups. The work suggests associations between gut microbial communities and tissue amino-acid profiles in poultry.

papers.title: Next-Generation Sequencing in Practical Wildlife Disease Investigation: Metagenomic Insights into European Bison and Gazelle Mortality and Morbidity Events.
papers.abstract: Wildlife disease investigations require diagnostic methods capable of detecting diverse and previously unrecognized pathogens. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was applied to samples from three Dorcas gazelles (Gazella dorcas osiris) affected by sudden mortality and four European bison (Bison bonasus) with respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis (NBP). No dominant bacterial species was detected in gazelles. In European bison, respiratory disease was associated with Pasteurella multocida, whereas NBP samples were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. Dorcas
papers.summary: This study applied metagenomic next-generation sequencing to investigate mortality and morbidity events in captive wildlife, analyzing samples from three Dorcas gazelles with sudden death and four European bison with respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis. No dominant bacterial pathogen was identified in the gazelles, while bison respiratory disease was linked to Pasteurella multocida and NBP samples were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. The work demonstrates that mNGS can provide actionable pathogen identification in practical wildlife disease investigations where conventional diagnostics fall short.

papers.title: Sketching the SRA: experiment-wide similarity search across 4.8 million metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Recent efforts have demonstrated that systematic analysis of the millions of metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) enables groundbreaking biological discoveries. However, SRA-scale comparison of whole metagenomes has remained elusive. Here, we introduce the most comprehensive resource to date for experiment-to-experiment analysis of all SRA metagenomes, comprising FracMinHash sketches (470GB), hypergen sketches (19GB), and an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix (90GB), which we release online at https://github.com/RolandFaure/SRA-metagenome-sketches-databases. These resources enable a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors created a comprehensive resource for comparing all 4.8 million metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive using compact FracMinHash and hypergen sketches, along with an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix. This enables experiment-to-experiment similarity search at SRA scale for the first time, opening the door to large-scale metagenomic discovery.

papers.title: Maternal transmission and limited virulent phage replication shape early infant gut virome maturation.
papers.abstract: Early life gut microbiome dynamics are increasingly recognized as important determinants of microbiome maturation, yet the ecological dynamics of its associated bacteriophages remain poorly resolved. Here, we performed bulk and virus like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling of longitudinal fecal samples from 32 mother-infant dyads, incorporating an exogenous phage spike in to enable absolute quantification of viral loads. Our results show that early infant gut phageome is defined by a profound lack of virulent phage genome copies while temperate phage
papers.summary: This study used longitudinal metagenomic sequencing with a known phage spike-in to absolutely quantify viral loads in 32 mother-infant pairs. It found that early infant gut phageomes are dominated by temperate phages with very few virulent phage genome copies, and that maternal transmission shapes the early virome, with limited virulent phage replication during infancy.

papers.title: Comparative Genomics of Ecologically Differentiated Nitrososphaera-Related Ammonia-Oxidizing Archaea.
papers.abstract: Soil acidification strongly influences the ecology of terrestrial ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA). Within this group, the Nitrososphaera-related alpha (NS-α) and delta (NS-δ) lineages exhibit pronounced pH-associated ecological differentiation. In the preceding microcosm experiment, NS-α populations showed greater persistence than NS-δ during ammonium-driven soil acidification, yet the genomic basis underlying this ecological differentiation remains poorly understood. In this study, metagenomic sequencing of one near-neutral baseline microcosm (pH 7.35) and one acidified microcosm (pH 4.73) wa
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing of soil microcosms at near-neutral (pH 7.35) and acidified (pH 4.73) conditions to compare the genomes of two ecologically differentiated ammonia-oxidizing archaeal lineages, NS-α and NS-δ. The authors identify genomic features that may explain why NS-α populations persist better than NS-δ under ammonium-driven acidification. The work links pH-associated ecological differentiation to underlying genomic differences in these soil AOA lineages.

papers.title: Complementary Use of Shotgun Metagenomics and Multiplex PCR for Pathogen Detection on High-Touch Surfaces.
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomics is being increasingly promoted as a pathogen-agnostic alternative to targeted PCR for environmental surveillance, yet its practical value on dry, low-biomass, host-dominated surfaces remains uncertain. In a companion study, we reported QIAstat-Dx multiplex PCR screening of 55 pooled high-touch surface samples from Riyadh, identifying 19 positive pools (34.5%). Here, in a retrospective exploratory comparison, we use those previously reported PCR calls as the targeted comparator and ask what unenriched shotgun metagenomic sequencing adds. Ten archived pools, each with at lea
papers.summary: This study retrospectively compared unenriched shotgun metagenomic sequencing against multiplex PCR for detecting pathogens on high-touch surfaces in Riyadh. Using ten archived PCR-positive pools as a comparator, the authors assessed what additional information metagenomics provides on dry, low-biomass, host-dominated surfaces. The work highlights the practical limitations and complementary value of pathogen-agnostic sequencing versus targeted PCR for environmental surveillance.

papers.title: Immunomodulatory and Metabolic Effects of Ginsenosides Rg1/Rb1 in IBD, RA, and MASLD: Targeting Gut Microbiota-Autoimmunity Axis.
papers.abstract: Panax ginseng Meyer has been commonly used as a traditional herbal medicine in East Asia for millennia. Ginsenosides Rg1 and Rb1 are the primary pharmacologically active ingredients and exhibit broad therapeutic efficacy against immunometabolic disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). To summarize the protective roles of these ginsenosides and investigate their underlying mechanisms, we integrated literature evidence with network pharmacology and gut microbiota-host gene association a
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that ginsenosides Rg1 and Rb1 from Panax ginseng alleviate inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Using network pharmacology and gut microbiota-host gene association analyses, the authors propose that these compounds act through immunomodulatory and metabolic pathways linked to the gut microbiota-autoimmunity axis. The work frames ginsenosides as multi-target modulators bridging microbial ecology and host immune-metabolic regulation.

papers.title: Human milk oligosaccharides are distinctly processed by early life gut microbial sialidases.
papers.abstract: The infant gut microbiome in early life is shaped by numerous factors, including feeding method. Exclusively breastfed and formula-fed infants exhibit distinct microbiome compositions. While these effects are well-established, the underlying mechanisms that drive these differences are not fully understood. Here, we examine the removal of sialic acid from human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) influenced by human microbial sialidases in early life. We identify 351 and 214 unique sialidase sequences from adult and infant microbiome metagenomes, respectively, and characterize a diverse, representativ
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes sialidase enzymes from early-life gut microbiomes that remove sialic acid from human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), revealing how infant gut microbes process these breast milk components differently than adult microbes. The authors catalogued 351 adult and 214 infant sialidase sequences and functionally characterized representative enzymes, showing distinct processing patterns that may help explain microbiome differences between breastfed and formula-fed infants.

papers.title: WasteFams: a database of protein families from global wastewater microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance has emerged as a critical tool for global epidemiology, yet the functional diversity of wastewater microbiomes remains poorly characterized at the protein level. Here, we present WasteFams, the first comprehensive database dedicated to the systematic exploration of protein families in wastewater metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies worldwide. Integrating data from 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (504 metagenomes, 129 metatranscriptomes, and 1151 reference genomes after filtering), WasteFams catalogs 3887 non-redundant protein fa
papers.summary: WasteFams is a new database cataloging protein families found in wastewater microbiomes worldwide, built by integrating 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (filtered to 504, 129, and 1151 respectively). It provides the first systematic protein-level characterization of wastewater microbial functional diversity, yielding 3887 non-redundant protein families. This resource supports wastewater surveillance and functional microbiome research.

papers.title: A systematic review of the effects of diet on the gut microbiota in individuals at elevated risk for colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) poses a major public health concern, with emerging evidence highlighting the critical role of the gut microbiota in CRC progression. Considering that diet is a major modifiable factor influencing CRC risk, partly through its interaction with the gut microbiome, this systematic review evaluated the effects of dietary intervention RCTs, including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns, on the gut microbiome in elevated-risk individuals.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines randomized controlled trials of dietary interventions—including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns—and their effects on the gut microbiome in people at elevated risk for colorectal cancer. It synthesizes evidence on how diet, a modifiable CRC risk factor, may shape the microbiome in this high-risk population.

papers.title: Co-occurrence and genetic contexts of NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1 carbapenemase genes in a critically ill patient.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant organisms are increasingly reported in clinical settings, yet the simultaneous detection of multiple carbapenemase genes within a single specimen remains rare.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This case report describes the rare simultaneous detection of four distinct carbapenemase genes (NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1) in a single critically ill patient, and analyzes their co-occurrence and genetic contexts. The finding highlights the potential for multidrug-resistant bacteria to accumulate multiple resistance determinants, complicating treatment and infection control.

papers.title: Why does apical periodontitis persist? A shotgun metagenomic survey of the microbial community in primary and persistent periapical granulomas.
papers.abstract: This cross‑sectional observational study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbiomes of periapical granulomas from primary and persistent apical periodontitis to identify microbial taxa and functional pathways associated with persistent lesions.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbial communities in periapical granulomas from primary versus persistent apical periodontitis, aiming to identify taxa and functional pathways linked to lesion persistence. The work provides a metagenomic characterization of these endodontic infections, potentially revealing microbial signatures that distinguish persistent from primary lesions.

papers.title: A Two-Stage ESM-Based Machine Learning Pipeline for Robust Hierarchically Evaluated Enzyme Function Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme annotation remains a major bottleneck in translating rapidly growing protein sequence data into biological knowledge. Enzyme Commission (EC) prediction is particularly challenging because enzyme functions are organized hierarchically, annotations are often imbalanced across classes, and sequence similarity alone may be insufficient to resolve functional differences. To address these challenges, we developed ESM-ECForest, a 2-stage framework that combines protein embeddings generated by the pretrained language model ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2) with random forest classi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-ECForest, a two-stage machine learning pipeline that uses protein language model embeddings from ESM-2 combined with random forest classifiers to predict Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. The hierarchical, two-stage design addresses class imbalance and the nested structure of enzyme function annotations, aiming to improve robustness over sequence-similarity-based approaches. This offers a practical route to annotate the growing backlog of uncharacterized protein sequences.

papers.title: Microbiome-driven precision psychiatry: integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and personalized interventions along the gut-brain axis.
papers.abstract: This scoping review maps evidence for microbiome-driven precision psychiatry in depression and anxiety.
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the evidence for using gut microbiome data to guide personalized treatment of depression and anxiety. It examines how multi-omics data, artificial intelligence, and gut-brain axis interventions could be integrated into precision psychiatry. The review highlights both the promise and the current gaps in translating microbiome research into clinical mental health care.

papers.title: Gut mycobiome dysbiosis in inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The intestinal mycobiome is increasingly recognized as an important component of host-microbiota interactions in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet its contribution to intestinal immune dysregulation remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize alterations in the intestinal mycobiome in patients with inflammatory bowel disease, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, compared with individuals without IBD, focusing on fungal diversity, taxonomic composition, and relative abundance, as well as their potential associations with disease phenotype and inflammatory activ
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis pools existing studies to characterize how the gut fungal community (mycobiome) differs between IBD patients and healthy controls. It examines fungal diversity, taxonomic composition, and abundance, and explores associations with disease phenotype and inflammation. The work consolidates evidence that fungal dysbiosis is a consistent feature of IBD, though the abstract does not report specific effect sizes.

papers.title: Phenotypic and genomic characterization of a halophilic sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfoplanes aerotolerans sp. nov. from a petroleum reservoir and its possible implication in pipeline corrosion.
papers.abstract: The issue of biogenic corrosion of steel equipment is especially pressing for petroleum reservoirs with high-salinity formation water containing sulfate. The predominance of sulfate-reducing bacteria of the genus Desulfoplanes in formation water samples from petroleum reservoirs in Tatarstan (Russia) was previously demonstrated using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomic analysis. The present study is devoted to the isolation, phenotypic and genomic characterization of the sulfate-reducing bacterial strain Desulfoplanes sp. PS50T and its involvement in steel corrosion. Studying the
papers.summary: The authors isolated and characterized a new halophilic sulfate-reducing bacterium, Desulfoplanes aerotolerans sp. nov. strain PS50T, from petroleum reservoir formation water in Tatarstan, Russia. Phenotypic and genomic analyses describe its salt tolerance, oxygen tolerance, and sulfate-reducing metabolism, and the study links the organism to steel corrosion relevant to pipeline integrity. The work extends prior 16S rRNA and metagenomic surveys that showed Desulfoplanes dominance in these high-salinity sulfate-rich environments.

papers.title: Gut microbiome taxonomic and functional capacity alterations in CHD and HFpEF.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is known to modulate metabolic health, yet its role in coronary heart disease (CHD) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains unclear. In the present study, we profiled the gut microbiome of 234 participants using shotgun metagenomic sequencing across controls (n = 43), individuals with low-risk atherosclerosis (LRAS, n = 23), and patients with CHD + HFpEF (n = 168). Species richness was significantly increased in CHD + HFpEF, with no disruption in taxonomic evenness. LRAS did not diverge significantly in alpha metrics. In contrast, beta diversity an
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic profiling of 234 participants reveals that patients with combined coronary heart disease and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (CHD+HFpEF) show significantly increased gut microbiome species richness without loss of taxonomic evenness, while low-risk atherosclerosis patients do not differ from controls in alpha diversity. Beta diversity and functional capacity analyses further distinguish the CHD+HFpEF group, suggesting disease-associated shifts in microbiome composition and metabolic potential.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing for culture-negative anaerobic central nervous system infection involving Prevotella oris: attribution challenges in low-biomass specimens.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic central nervous system (CNS) infections are uncommon but diagnostically difficult because fastidious organisms may be suppressed by empirical antimicrobial therapy and conventional cultures may remain negative. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can recover microbial nucleic acids in this setting, but low microbial biomass creates a central attribution problem: a detected organism may represent active infection, introduced commensal DNA, laboratory background, or bioinformatic misclassification. This narrative Mini Review uses Prevotella oris as a
papers.summary: This mini-review examines the diagnostic challenge of using cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to identify anaerobic CNS infections when conventional cultures are negative, using Prevotella oris as a case example. The authors highlight that low microbial biomass in CSF creates a fundamental attribution problem—a detected organism could reflect true infection, introduced commensal DNA, laboratory contamination, or bioinformatic misclassification. The review discusses strategies for interpreting mNGS results in this ambiguous context.

papers.title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical.
papers.summary: gTranslate is a new tool that predicts the correct genetic code (translation table) for prokaryotic genomes directly from sequence data, without requiring prior taxonomic classification. This addresses a common bottleneck in gene prediction pipelines, where the translation table must otherwise be specified manually or guessed via heuristics. The tool is presented as rapid and accurate, improving automation of prokaryotic genome annotation.

papers.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of the early gut microbiota development in Nipponia nippon.
papers.abstract: The crested ibis (Nipponia nippon) is an endangered bird whose early gut microbiota development remains poorly understood. To address this gap, this study integrated metagenomics and metabolomics to investigate the dynamic succession of gut microbiota and metabolism in naturally hatched chicks during early development.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics and metabolomics to track how the gut microbiota and metabolic profiles of endangered crested ibis chicks change during early development. It provides one of the first integrated characterizations of microbial succession in this species, offering baseline data that could inform conservation and captive-rearing strategies.

papers.title: Metagenomic and culture-dependent characterization of between-field variation in phosphorus-cycling microbial communities and functional potential across tobacco-safflower rotation fields.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms contribute to soil phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P acquisition, but P-cycling microbial communities and functional associations across tobacco-safflower rotation fields remain poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study combines metagenomic sequencing with culture-based methods to characterize phosphorus-cycling microbial communities in the rhizosphere across tobacco-safflower rotation fields, examining how these communities and their functional potential vary between fields. The work provides a baseline characterization of P-cycling taxa and genes in this rotation system, which has been poorly studied.

papers.title: Dietary exogenous microRNAs in the gut: biological effects, mechanistic evidence, and controversies.
papers.abstract: Dietary exogenous microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as potential mediators of interorganismal communication, with growing interest in their ability to influence gastrointestinal physiology and the gut microbiota. These molecules encompass plant-derived miRNAs implicated in cross-kingdom regulation, animal-derived dietary miRNAs involved in cross-species communication, and maternal milk miRNAs that may participate in mother-to-offspring molecular crosstalk. A proportion of dietary miRNAs are associated with extracellular vesicles or other protective complexes, which may enhance their stability du
papers.summary: This review examines evidence that microRNAs from food—including plant, animal, and milk-derived miRNAs—can survive digestion and influence gut physiology and the gut microbiota, potentially acting as cross-kingdom or cross-species signaling molecules. It discusses how some dietary miRNAs are packaged in extracellular vesicles or protective complexes that may enhance their stability, while also addressing ongoing controversies about whether these effects are biologically meaningful.

papers.title: Building biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota: methodological considerations, current challenges, and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiota (HGM) plays a pivotal role in human health by regulating metabolic, immune, and neurological processes and contributes to the susceptibility to various diseases. The increasing interest in microbiota-targeted therapies has highlighted the need for in vitro models capable of accurately reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem. This review examines the methodological factors that determine the biological relevance of HGM in vitro models, emphasizing that reliable experimental outcomes depend not only on the choi
papers.summary: This review examines the methodological factors that determine how biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota can be, arguing that reliable experimental results depend on more than just the choice of model system. It discusses current challenges in reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem and outlines future perspectives for improving these models.

papers.title: Interpretable detection-based image classification for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using smartphone-assisted microscopy.
papers.abstract: The vaginal discharge is a common clinical presentation associated with diverse infectious and microbiota-related conditions. Existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic approaches have predominantly focused on detection of individual pathogens and have rarely integrated microbiota-associated conditions within a diagnostic framework. We developed an explainable deep learning framework for automated analysis of Gram-stained vaginal smear images acquired using handheld smartphones or tablets positioned over a conventional light microscope eyepiece.
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable deep learning framework that analyzes Gram-stained vaginal smear images captured through a smartphone or tablet mounted on a conventional light microscope. Unlike prior AI tools that only detect individual pathogens, this system aims to support differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge by also incorporating microbiota-associated conditions, with interpretability built in.

papers.title: Gut microbiome and gut-derived metabolites to identify the transition from metabolically healthy to unhealthy obesity: a mini review.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a metabolically heterogeneous condition with distinct metabolic phenotypes, ranging from metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) to metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). Although individuals with MHO initially lack cardiometabolic dysfunction, many transition to MUO over time, exponentially increasing their risk for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. In this mini-review, we synthesize recent evidence from multi-omic cohort studies evaluating gut microbiome composition and gut-derived metabolites as functional biomarkers of obesity heterogeneity and drivers of metabolic decline
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes evidence from multi-omic cohort studies on how gut microbiome composition and gut-derived metabolites may serve as biomarkers distinguishing metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) from metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO) and as drivers of the transition between these states. The authors argue that microbiome and metabolite profiles could help identify individuals at risk of progressing to MUO, potentially enabling earlier intervention to reduce type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease risk.

papers.title: Investigating the Effect of Oral Probiotic Capsules on Postpartum Sleep Quality in Primiparous Women: A triple-blind randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Quality of sleep is an important indicator of health. Sleep disturbance and daytime fatigue is one of the most common problems in the postpartum period. Early postpartum (first 4 weeks) is when sleep is most disturbed. The gut microbiota may affect sleep quality and affect host health through the production of metabolites and compounds. This study aimed to determine the effect of oral probiotic capsule on the quality of sleep after delivery in primiparous women.
papers.summary: This triple-blind randomized controlled trial tested whether oral probiotic capsules improve sleep quality in first-time mothers during the early postpartum period, when sleep disturbance is most common. The rationale is that gut microbiota may influence sleep via metabolite production. The abstract does not report results, so the key finding cannot yet be assessed.

papers.title: Evaluating traditional Chinese medicine modulation of the gut microbiota-bile acid axis in metabolic and inflammatory diseases: mechanistic evidence and translational priorities.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D), and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are clinically distinct disorders that share perturbations in intestinal ecology, bile-acid composition, epithelial barrier function, and immune-metabolic regulation. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) may modify these interconnected processes, but the translational significance of reported effects remains uncertain. Changes in microbial composition are often interpreted as mechanisms without evidence of altered microbial function, bile-acid profiles o
papers.summary: This review examines how traditional Chinese medicine may influence metabolic and inflammatory diseases (MASLD, obesity, T2D, IBD) through the gut microbiota–bile acid axis. The authors argue that many reported microbial shifts are over-interpreted as mechanisms without functional or bile-acid evidence, and they outline translational priorities to strengthen causal claims.

papers.title: Metabolomics in the wild: A scoping review of non-invasive methods for understanding vertebrate wildlife health and success.
papers.abstract: An increase in metabolomics research over the last decade has expanded species-specific knowledge of biological processes, but has primarily focused upon humans, domesticated and model animal species. Recent advances, particularly around data management pipelines for untargeted studies, make the field more accessible to disciplines outside those embedded in analytical chemistry, including wildlife conservation. To establish the breadth of existing wild vertebrate animal metabolomic research, specifically utilising non-invasive sampling, this scoping review establishes: (1) general trends in pu
papers.summary: This scoping review surveys the use of non-invasive metabolomics sampling methods in wild vertebrate animals, a field that has lagged behind human and model-organism metabolomics. It maps general trends in publication and identifies gaps in how untargeted metabolomics pipelines are applied to wildlife health and conservation questions. The work highlights that improved data-management pipelines are making metabolomics more accessible to conservation researchers.
